topic: HER2 positive breast cancer adjuvant trastuzumab

page.mentor_intro: HER2-positive breast cancer used to be the aggressive subtype; adjuvant trastuzumab turned it into one of the more curable ones. About 15-20% of breast cancers overexpress HER2, and adding trastuzumab to chemotherapy produced one of the largest survival benefits ever recorded in adjuvant oncology. The modern craft is duration and escalation: one year of trastuzumab as the default, neoadjuvant therapy when downsizing matters, and escalation to dual HER2 blockade or T-DM1 for residual disease after neoadjuvant treatment.

teaching_points.claim: About 15% to 20% of breast cancers are HER2-positive — a more aggressive subtype with shortened survival; meta-analysis evidence defines the optimal adjuvant trastuzumab regimen.
The availability of HER2-targeted therapy has dramatically improved outcomes in HER2-positive early breast cancer, as demonstrated by the EBCTCG meta-analysis on trastuzumab.
Anti-HER2 treatment has changed the natural biology of HER2-positive breast cancer, with major achievements in both metastatic and early disease and particular success of neoadjuvant approaches.
Adjuvant and neoadjuvant breast cancer treatments reduce breast cancer mortality, though effects on other-cause mortality vary — a systematic review quantified these trade-offs.

standard_knowledge.claim: HER2 amplification or overexpression occurs in about 15 to 20% of breast cancers; anti-HER2 monoclonal antibodies have transformed outcomes in the neoadjuvant, adjuvant and metastatic settings.

uncertainties: De-escalation questions — shorter trastuzumab duration for selected low-risk patients, and chemotherapy-free regimens for small node-negative tumours — remain partially unresolved.
Optimal escalation for residual disease after neoadjuvant therapy continues to evolve with newer agents.
mcq_angles: The magnitude of adjuvant trastuzumab benefit and its evidence base (EBCTCG meta-analysis).
One-year versus shorter durations: what trials showed.
Neoadjuvant therapy and pathologic complete response as a prognostic and escalation trigger.
Cardiac monitoring during HER2 therapy (LVEF surveillance).

topic: hypercalcaemia of malignancy

page.mentor_intro: Hypercalcaemia of malignancy is the commonest metabolic complication of cancer and the commonest cause of hypercalcaemia in hospitalised patients, affecting over a quarter of patients with cancer across its phenotypes — humoral (PTHrP-driven), osteolytic, and the rarer calcitriol-secreting and ectopic-PTH forms. Its epidemiology is shifting: incidence may be declining as cancer therapy improves, and mortality from HCM has fallen markedly with effective chemotherapy. Acute management remains hydration plus an antiresorptive — bisphosphonate or denosumab — with treatment of the underlying malignancy as the definitive lever.

teaching_points.claim: An Endocrine Society clinical practice guideline addresses treatment of hypercalcemia of malignancy in adults; HCM is the most common metabolic complication of malignancy, with incidence possibly declining due to potent chemotherapeutic agents.
HCM affects over a quarter of patients being treated for cancer, with humoral, osteolytic, ectopic-hyperparathyroidism and vitamin-D-secreting lymphoma mechanisms.
Cancer-related hypercalcemia occurs in about 20–30% of patients with advanced cancer and is the most common cause of hypercalcemia in hospitalised patients.

standard_knowledge.claim: For hypercalcaemia of malignancy refractory to intravenous bisphosphonates (zoledronic acid 4 mg), denosumab 120 mg subcutaneously lowers calcium and is preferred in renal impairment, where bisphosphonates need dose caution.

uncertainties: Choosing between bisphosphonates and denosumab — including cost, renal function constraints and hypocalcaemia risk — is individualised.
How emerging cancer therapies are reshaping HCM incidence and prognosis is an evolving picture.

topic: Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis variants by antigen

page.mentor_intro: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis is not one disease but a family of them, and the antigen defines the member: bird fancier's lung, farmer's lung, hot-tub lung and the summer-type HP of humid climates each carry their own exposure pattern, clinical phenotype and prognosis. Systematic curation of reported HP-associated exposures — long missing — now underpins confident antigen identification, which remains the single most valuable diagnostic and therapeutic act in the disease, because removal of the right exposure is the only intervention that changes the natural history.

teaching_points.claim: A scoping review systematically identified reported exposures associated with HP and their clinical phenotypes, addressing the absence of curated exposure lists to inform diagnosis.

Major occupational and domestic triggers include avian antigens (pigeon, parakeet, and goose-feather bedding causing bird fancier's lung) and thermophilic actinomycetes (Saccharopolyspora rectivirgula in moldy hay causing farmer's lung).

Industrial exposure variants include isocyanate-induced HP in spray painters, metalworking fluid HP ('machine operator's lung'), and cheese washer's lung (Penicillium roqueforti), highlighting the necessity of detailed occupational histories.

standard_knowledge.claim: Prognosis strongly correlates with specific causative antigens and host clearance: avian antigen exposure and occult domestic exposures carry higher risks of progression to irreversible pulmonary fibrosis than episodic farming antigens.

uncertainties: Many HP patients have no identifiable antigen despite systematic exposure assessment, limiting phenotype-based prognosis.
The strength of association between specific antigens and fibrotic versus non-fibrotic courses is incompletely quantified.

topic: Hypertensive Nephrosclerosis

page.mentor_intro: Hypertensive nephrosclerosis — nephroangiosclerosis — is the kidney disease that accompanies chronic essential hypertension, known for over a century and still diagnosed more by clinical context than by biopsy, which is reserved for doubtful or atypical cases. The clinical picture is one of slowly progressive chronic kidney disease with subnephrotic proteinuria in a patient with long-standing, often poorly controlled hypertension. The modern nuance is that the causal arrow is not always simple: some 'hypertensive' nephrosclerosis may reflect primary renal microvascular disease driving the hypertension rather than vice versa, particularly in certain ancestries.

teaching_points.claim: Nephroangiosclerosis — kidney disease accompanying chronic essential hypertension — has been recognised for over a century; definitive diagnosis is by renal biopsy, reserved for doubtful or atypical cases.

Pathologically, chronic arteriolosclerosis is characterized by medial hypertrophy, intimal hyalinosis of afferent arterioles, and downstream ischemic glomerulosclerosis, leading to progressive non-proteinuric or subnephrotic renal decline.

High-risk APOL1 genetic variants (G1 and G2 alleles) strongly predispose individuals of African ancestry to accelerated hypertensive nephrosclerosis and aggressive progression toward end-stage renal disease.

standard_knowledge.claim: Blood pressure control with a RAAS inhibitor (target below 130/80 mmHg; KDIGO suggests systolic below 120 mmHg with standardised measurement) plus sodium restriction (under 2 g/day) is the cornerstone of renal protection.

uncertainties: The bidirectionality question — whether renal microvascular disease precedes hypertension in some patients — is unresolved.
Whether aggressive BP control halts established nephrosclerosis beyond general CKD benefit is inferred rather than proven.
mcq_angles: Clinical diagnostic pattern: CKD plus chronic hypertension plus subnephrotic proteinuria.
When biopsy is indicated (atypical features, active urinary sediment).
Differential: other secondary hypertension causes with renal involvement.
Management as CKD with strict BP control and renin-angiotensin blockade.

topic: Hyperthyroidism: Graves disease vs toxic nodular goitre, TSH receptor antibodies

page.mentor_intro: Separating Graves' disease from toxic nodular goitre is the pivotal fork in thyrotoxicosis management, and the ATA guideline supplies the algorithm. Both share suppressed TSH and elevated hormones; they diverge on TRAb — positive in Graves', negative in nodular disease — and on the radionuclide uptake scan, which shows diffuse uptake in Graves' versus patchy or focal uptake in toxic nodular goitre. The distinction is not academic: Graves' warrants consideration of antithyroid drugs as first-line with thionamide complications in view, while toxic nodular goitre virtually never remits on drugs and heads toward radioiodine or surgery.

teaching_points.claim: The ATA guideline describes evidence-based diagnosis and management of hyperthyroidism and other causes of thyrotoxicosis, where appropriate treatment requires accurate diagnosis and is influenced by comorbidity and patient preference.

Thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor antibodies (TRAb / TSI) demonstrate >97-99% sensitivity and specificity for diagnosing Graves' disease, distinguishing it from toxic nodular goitre and destructive thyroiditis without radioiodine uptake scans.

Toxic multinodular goitre and solitary toxic adenoma are caused by activating TSH-receptor somatic mutations; unlike Graves' disease, they never remit spontaneously and require definitive therapy (radioactive iodine or surgical resection).

standard_knowledge.claim: First-line antithyroid drug therapy for Graves' disease is methimazole (MMI), except during the first trimester of pregnancy or in thyroid storm where propylthiouracil (PTU) is preferred due to MMI-associated embryopathy.

uncertainties: TRAb-negative thyrotoxicosis sometimes needs imaging to resolve the aetiology, and uptake scans are contraindicated in pregnancy.
Whether Graves' first-line should be thionamides or radioiodine varies by guideline, geography and patient factors.
mcq_angles: TRAb testing as the first-line differentiator.
Uptake-scan patterns: diffuse (Graves') versus focal (toxic nodular).

topic: IBD in Pregnancy

page.mentor_intro: The single most important fact about IBD in pregnancy is that active disease harms the pregnancy far more than the medications do: quiescent disease at conception predicts a smooth course, while active flares drive preterm birth, low birth weight and pregnancy loss. The therapeutic implication runs against maternal instinct but with the evidence: continue 5-ASA, thiopurines and biologics through conception and pregnancy, adjust anti-TNF scheduling around the third trimester, and avoid methotrexate entirely. Preconception disease control is the intervention that changes outcomes.

teaching_points.claim: Ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease are chronic heterogeneous inflammatory conditions of the gastrointestinal tract; BSG consensus guidelines provide adult management frameworks relevant to pregnancy planning and care.

Maintaining remission prior to conception and throughout gestation is paramount; active maternal bowel inflammation confers a substantially greater risk of miscarriage, preterm delivery, and low birth weight than guideline maintenance medications.

Biologic therapies (anti-TNF agents: infliximab, adalimumab; vedolizumab; ustekinumab) are generally safe throughout pregnancy, with active transplacental transfer occurring predominantly in the third trimester via fetal Fc receptors.

standard_knowledge.claim: Methotrexate is absolutely contraindicated during pregnancy and conception (teratogenic embryopathy); tofacitinib should be avoided, whereas thiopurines (azathioprine) and 5-ASAs (except those with dibutyl phthalate coating) are safe to continue.

uncertainties: Optimal anti-TNF drug-level monitoring and third-trimester dosing schedules vary by agent and guideline.
Small-molecule (JAK/S1P) safety data in pregnancy remain limited.
mcq_angles: Drug safety ladder in pregnancy: safe, schedule-adjusted, contraindicated.
Disease activity at conception as the outcome driver.
Mode-of-delivery considerations with perianal Crohn's.

topic: Latent autoimmune diabetes in adults LADA: GAD antibodies, insulin progression

page.mentor_intro: Latent autoimmune diabetes in adults (LADA) presents phenotypically as type 2 diabetes but features islet autoantibodies and progressive immune-mediated pancreatic beta-cell destruction. Clinical decision-making balances early glycemic control with beta-cell preservation, guided by baseline GADA titers and residual C-peptide secretion.

teaching_points.claim: The 2020 international expert consensus on LADA establishes that screening for glutamic acid decarboxylase autoantibodies (GADA) is recommended in adults presenting with apparent type 2 diabetes who are non-obese, age under 50, or exhibit early oral agent failure.

Residual fasting C-peptide concentrations stratify therapeutic pathways in LADA: levels below 0.3 nmol/L require an immediate multiple-dose insulin regimen, while levels from 0.3 to 0.7 nmol/L represent a vulnerable gray zone where insulin is introduced or combined with incretin therapies.

Sulfonylureas are contraindicated or strongly discouraged in LADA as secretagogues accelerate autoimmune beta-cell apoptosis and hasten progression toward complete insulin dependence compared to insulin or metformin.

standard_knowledge.claim: High-titre GAD antibody positivity, especially with multiple islet antibodies, predicts faster beta-cell loss, and most patients with LADA need insulin within a few years of diagnosis.

uncertainties: Whether upfront immunomodulatory interventions (such as low-dose alum-formulated GAD65) can permanently halt progressive beta-cell decline in newly diagnosed LADA cohorts.
The long-term renal and cardiovascular outcomes of SGLT2 inhibitors in LADA patients with intermediate C-peptide levels due to euglycemic DKA risk.
mcq_angles: Diagnostic criteria differentiating LADA from classic adult-onset type 1 and type 2 diabetes (age >=30, presence of islet autoantibodies, and at least 6 months without initial insulin requirement).
Selection of optimal pharmacotherapy when C-peptide is 0.4 nmol/L (avoiding sulfonylureas, combining metformin/incretins with low-dose basal insulin).
Autoantibody panel priority: high sensitivity and diagnostic utility of GADA over IA-2A and ZnT8 in adult populations.

topic: latent tuberculosis

page.mentor_intro: Latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) represents a state of persistent immune response to Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigens without evidence of clinically active disease. Clinical management prioritizes identifying high-risk individuals for progression, excluding active pulmonary or extrapulmonary disease, and selecting short-course rifamycin regimens.

teaching_points.claim: The 2020 CDC and NTCA guidelines preferentially recommend short-course rifamycin-based regimens over 6- to 9-month isoniazid monotherapy for treating latent tuberculosis infection due to superior completion rates and reduced hepatotoxicity.

Active tuberculosis disease must be definitively excluded via targeted symptom screening and chest radiography before commencing any latent TB regimen to prevent the rapid emergence of rifamycin resistance.

standard_knowledge.claim: Interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs) demonstrate superior diagnostic specificity over the tuberculin skin test (TST) in individuals with prior BCG vaccination or non-tuberculous mycobacterial exposures.

The randomized PREVENT TB trial confirmed that 3 months of once-weekly isoniazid plus rifapentine (3HP) is noninferior to 9 months of daily isoniazid, with treatment completion rates of 82.1% versus 69.0%.

uncertainties: The optimal screening and preventive treatment strategy for individuals repeatedly exposed to multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) contacts.
Safety and efficacy of ultra-short 1-month regimens (1HP) in immunocompetent non-HIV adult populations.
mcq_angles: Distinguishing LTBI from active tuberculosis: positive IGRA with normal chest radiograph and absent constitutional symptoms vs active cavitation.
First-line regimen selection in a patient initiating TNF-alpha inhibitor therapy: preferential use of 3HP or 4R over 9H.
Management of elevated baseline transaminases during rifamycin treatment and absolute thresholds for therapy discontinuation.

topic: Latent tuberculosis infection treatment

page.mentor_intro: Latent tuberculosis infection treatment prevents progression to active disease in high-risk hosts. Modern guidelines prioritize 3- to 4-month rifamycin-containing options (3HP, 4R, 3HR) over protracted isoniazid monotherapies, balancing cytochrome P450 interactions and hepatic tolerance.

teaching_points.claim: The preferred first-line options for latent tuberculosis in the 2020 CDC/NTCA guidelines are 3 months of once-weekly isoniazid plus rifapentine (3HP) or 4 months of daily rifampin monotherapy (4R).

Rifamycins are potent inducers of CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein, necessitating close dosage adjustment or alternative regimens for patients taking protease inhibitors, direct oral anticoagulants, or calcineurin inhibitors.

3HP can be co-administered with efavirenz- or dolutegravir-based antiretroviral therapy, which widens access to short-course treatment of latent TB in people with HIV.

topic: Late-onset hypogonadism: diagnostic thresholds, testosterone replacement risks, monitoring

page.mentor_intro: Late-onset hypogonadism involves persistent clinical features of androgen deficiency paired with unequivocally low serum testosterone levels in aging men. The Endocrine Society emphasizes rigorous morning laboratory verification, exclusion of reversible secondary etiologies, and objective cardiovascular risk evaluation.

teaching_points.claim: The Endocrine Society clinical guideline requires at least two separate fasting morning (8:00 AM to 10:00 AM) total testosterone measurements below 300 ng/dL (10.4 nmol/L) alongside specific clinical symptoms to establish a diagnosis of hypogonadism.

The randomized TRAVERSE trial of 5,246 hypogonadal men with cardiovascular disease or high risk showed that transdermal testosterone therapy was noninferior to placebo for major adverse cardiovascular events (HR 0.96; 95% CI, 0.78 to 1.17).

Baseline and surveillance monitoring during testosterone replacement requires periodic hematocrit assessment to detect polycythemia, with treatment withholding or dose reduction recommended if hematocrit exceeds 54%.

standard_knowledge.claim: In the TRAVERSE trial, testosterone therapy did not reduce clinical fracture risk and was unexpectedly associated with a numerically higher incidence of all clinical fractures compared with placebo (HR 1.43).

uncertainties: The precise biological mechanism responsible for increased clinical fracture incidence observed in elderly men receiving transdermal testosterone in the TRAVERSE trial.
Long-term prostate cancer incidence and progression rates beyond 5 years of therapeutic testosterone replacement in men with treated low-risk localized prostate carcinoma.
mcq_angles: Diagnostic confirmation of hypogonadism: necessity of repeat morning fasting total testosterone and evaluating free testosterone if SHBG is altered.
Cardiovascular safety consensus following TRAVERSE: non-inferiority for MACE but increased risk of arrhythmias (atrial fibrillation), venous thromboembolism, and acute kidney injury.
Mandatory lab safety threshold for erythrocytosis: dose reduction or phlebotomy if hematocrit exceeds 54%.

topic: Lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow): assessment and management

page.mentor_intro: Lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow) is a chronic angiofibroblastic tendinopathy of the common extensor origin, primarily involving the extensor carpi radialis brevis (ECRB). Management focuses on eccentric wrist extensor rehabilitation, while reserving interventional therapies for refractory pain.

teaching_points.claim: A 2023 meta-analysis of Level 1 and 2 randomized trials established that corticosteroid injections are superior to platelet-rich plasma (PRP) at 1 month, whereas PRP achieves superior and durable functional and pain scores at 6 months.

standard_knowledge.claim: Randomised trials (Bisset BMJ 2006; Coombes JAMA 2013) show corticosteroid injection gives better pain relief at about 4 weeks but worse outcomes and more recurrence at 6 to 12 months than physiotherapy, wait-and-see or placebo.

A randomized controlled trial in the BMJ demonstrated that physical therapy combining elbow mobilization with movement and eccentric exercise yields superior durable long-term success at 52 weeks compared with corticosteroid injection.

Pathologically, lateral epicondylitis represents non-inflammatory angiofibroblastic tendinosis and collagen disorientation rather than acute inflammation, explaining the limited disease-modifying utility of chronic oral NSAIDs.

uncertainties: The comparative clinical efficacy of leukocyte-rich versus leukocyte-poor platelet-rich plasma formulations in chronic refractory tendinopathy.
The optimal timing and definitive clinical indication for surgical or arthroscopic ECRB debridement after failed conservative therapy.
mcq_angles: Clinical physical exam localization: maximal point tenderness 1 to 2 cm distal to the lateral epicondyle exacerbated by resisted wrist and third digit extension.
Long-term therapeutic trajectory of local corticosteroid injections: transient early relief followed by high recurrence and tendon matrix compromise at 12 months.
First-line evidence-based conservative management: heavy slow resistance/eccentric wrist extensor physiotherapy combined with activity modification.

topic: LDL lowering and ASCVD prevention

page.mentor_intro: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk reduction is fundamentally driven by absolute low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) reduction. Landmark trials and current guidelines establish that lower LDL-C levels achieved over long durations yield progressive reductions in major adverse cardiovascular events without an identified lower safety threshold.

teaching_points.claim: The IMPROVE-IT trial established that adding ezetimibe to simvastatin in post-acute coronary syndrome patients lowered median LDL-C to 53.7 mg/dL and significantly reduced major adverse cardiovascular events (HR 0.936, P=0.016), validating non-statin LDL lowering.

The FOURIER trial demonstrated that adding the PCSK9 inhibitor evolocumab to statin therapy lowered LDL-C to a median of 30 mg/dL and significantly reduced the composite of cardiovascular death, MI, stroke, hospitalization for angina, or revascularization (HR 0.85, P<0.001).

The 2019 ESC/EAS guidelines establish an intensive LDL-C goal of <55 mg/dL (<1.4 mmol/L) alongside at least a 50% baseline reduction for individuals at very high cardiovascular risk, recommending a stepwise addition of ezetimibe and PCSK9 inhibitors.

standard_knowledge.claim: ODYSSEY OUTCOMES showed that alirocumab added to high-intensity statin after acute coronary syndrome reduced major cardiovascular events (HR 0.85) and, in a nominal analysis, all-cause death, with the greatest benefit when baseline LDL-C was 100 mg/dL or higher.

uncertainties: Long-term neurocognitive and endocrine safety profiles when sustaining ultra-low LDL-C levels (<20 mg/dL) over decades with combination siRNA (inclisiran) and PCSK9 inhibitors.
The incremental benefit and cost-effectiveness of routine triple therapy (statin + ezetimibe + PCSK9 inhibitor) initiated upfront during index acute myocardial infarction hospitalization.
mcq_angles: Target LDL-C thresholds in very-high-risk secondary prevention: <55 mg/dL (1.4 mmol/L) and >=50% baseline reduction.
Mechanism of ezetimibe: selective inhibition of the Niemann-Pick C1-Like 1 (NPC1L1) transporter at the intestinal brush border.
Interpretation of landmark PCSK9 inhibitor trials: significant reduction in ischemic events with no increase in neurocognitive dysfunction or hemorrhagic stroke.

topic: Leishmaniasis: visceral vs cutaneous, kala-azar, liposomal amphotericin B, diagnosis

page.mentor_intro: Leishmaniasis encompasses a clinical spectrum ranging from self-limiting cutaneous lesions to life-threatening visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) caused by Leishmania donovani and L. infantum. Management requires prompt parasitological or serological diagnosis and species-directed antiparasitic chemotherapy.

teaching_points.claim: Visceral leishmaniasis is characterized by the clinical triad of prolonged irregular fever, progressive hepatosplenomegaly, and pancytopenia, coupled with hypergammaglobulinemia and severe wasting.

standard_knowledge.claim: The World Health Organization and IDSA guidelines recommend liposomal amphotericin B as the treatment of choice for visceral leishmaniasis, achieving cure rates exceeding 95% with significantly lower nephrotoxicity than conventional amphotericin B deoxycholate.

In HIV-associated visceral leishmaniasis, liposomal amphotericin B combined with miltefosine may reduce relapse compared with amphotericin alone (small trial data); secondary prophylaxis is also needed.

Diagnosis rests on finding Leishmania amastigotes in splenic, bone marrow or lymph node aspirates; the rK39 rapid antibody test is useful in immunocompetent patients in South Asia but less sensitive in East Africa and in HIV co-infection.

uncertainties: The optimal secondary chemoprophylaxis regimen and duration to prevent visceral leishmaniasis relapses in patients living with HIV who have severe CD4 count suppression.
Efficacy and tolerability of oral miltefosine in young children under 2 years of age with visceral leishmaniasis.
mcq_angles: Identification of Leishmania amastigotes (LD bodies) within macrophages on bone marrow aspirate smear using Giemsa stain.
First-line treatment of choice for kala-azar in South Asia: single-dose (10 mg/kg) liposomal amphotericin B.
Diagnostic limitations of rK39 serology: false-negative tests in HIV-coinfected patients due to impaired antibody production, requiring direct bone marrow aspiration.

topic: Leptomeningeal Disease

page.mentor_intro: Leptomeningeal metastasis represents diffuse tumor dissemination into the arachnoid membrane and cerebrospinal fluid, carrying a devastating prognosis. The 2023 EANO-ESMO guidelines emphasize multimodality management combining modern CNS-penetrant targeted therapies, focal radiation, and selective intrathecal pharmacotherapy.

teaching_points.claim: The 2023 EANO-ESMO clinical practice guideline establishes that contrast-enhanced thin-slice whole neuroaxis MRI and CSF cytology are the gold standard diagnostic investigations for suspected leptomeningeal metastasis.

In patients with EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer and leptomeningeal metastases, the third-generation EGFR-TKI osimertinib (including high-dose 160 mg daily regimens) demonstrates profound CNS penetration with objective CSF and neurological response rates.

Intrathecal chemotherapy (methotrexate, liposomal cytarabine, or pemetrexed) via an Ommaya reservoir is indicated primarily for diffuse linear cytologic disease without bulky nodular masses or CSF flow obstruction confirmed on radioisotope cisternography.

standard_knowledge.claim: Focal radiotherapy is recommended to alleviate focal symptomatic cranial neuropathies, painful cauda equina nerve root compressions, or to relieve localized CSF flow obstructions prior to initiating intrathecal therapies.

uncertainties: The optimal integration and sequencing of systemic antibody-drug conjugates (such as trastuzumab deruxtecan) versus intrathecal targeted therapies in HER2-positive breast cancer leptomeningeal disease.
Clinical utility of CSF circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) liquid biopsy for therapeutic response monitoring compared to standard serial cytomorphology.
mcq_angles: Diagnostic confirmation of leptomeningeal disease: finding malignant cells in CSF and linear leptomeningeal contrast enhancement on gadolinium-enhanced brain and spine MRI.
Mandatory step prior to instilling intrathecal chemotherapy: performing CSF flow scintigraphy to rule out obstructive flow blocks that cause toxic local pooling.
Selection of CNS-penetrant targeted therapy for driver-mutated solid tumors (e.g. osimertinib for EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma).
case_hooks: A 54-year-old female with metastatic breast cancer presenting with multifocal neurological deficits, including horizontal diplopia, progressive headache, and bilateral lower extremity radicular weakness.
A 62-year-old non-smoker with known EGFR L858R lung adenocarcinoma on standard osimertinib 80 mg presenting with new-onset seizures and linear leptomeningeal enhancement.

topic: Lewy body dementia diagnosis and symptomatic therapy

page.mentor_intro: Dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) is the second most common neurodegenerative dementia in older adults. The 4th Consensus Report of the DLB Consortium establishes clinical criteria, validates indicative biomarkers, and outlines careful symptomatic pharmacotherapy emphasizing extreme sensitivity to neuroleptic agents.

teaching_points.claim: The 2017 Fourth Consensus Report of the DLB Consortium defines probable DLB by the presence of two or more core clinical features: fluctuating cognition with pronounced variations in attention, recurrent formed visual hallucinations, REM sleep behavior disorder, and spontaneous parkinsonism.

Indicative biomarkers that confirm DLB in the presence of one core clinical feature include reduced dopamine transporter (DAT) uptake in the basal ganglia on SPECT/PET, reduced 123I-MIBG myocardial scintigraphy, and polysomnographic confirmation of REM sleep without atonia.

Cholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil and rivastigmine) are first-line pharmacotherapies in DLB, providing significant improvements in global cognitive function, apathy, and neuropsychiatric symptoms by addressing profound cortical cholinergic deficits.

standard_knowledge.claim: Conventional (first-generation) antipsychotics should be avoided in dementia with Lewy bodies because of severe neuroleptic sensitivity reactions, including worsened parkinsonism, neuroleptic malignant syndrome and higher mortality; if essential, use very low-dose quetiapine, clozapine or pimavanserin.

uncertainties: The clinical utility of low-dose quetiapine versus pimavanserin for managing distressing hallucinations refractory to cholinesterase inhibitors in DLB.
Disease-modifying potential of anti-alpha-synuclein monoclonal antibodies currently in early-phase clinical development.
mcq_angles: Application of the McKeith 2017 criteria: differentiating DLB from Parkinson's disease dementia using the 1-year rule (cognitive impairment preceding or within 1 year of motor parkinsonism).
Pharmacological risk: severe neuroleptic sensitivity induced by typical antipsychotics (e.g. haloperidol).
Indicative diagnostic biomarkers for DLB: DAT-SPECT showing loss of putaminal tracer uptake and cardiac MIBG scintigraphy demonstrating sympathetic denervation.

A 75-year-old female with mild Parkinsonism who is prescribed haloperidol for acute nocturnal agitation in the hospital and subsequently becomes catatonic and rigid with acute hyperthermia.

topic: Liberation from mechanical ventilation: weaning protocols

page.mentor_intro: Liberation from mechanical ventilation requires systematic daily assessment of extubation readiness to avoid complications of prolonged intubation or premature extubation. The ATS/CHEST guidelines recommend protocolized spontaneous breathing trials (SBTs) with inspiratory pressure augmentation over unassisted T-piece trials.

teaching_points.claim: Protocol-driven weaning led by respiratory therapists and nurses significantly reduces mechanical ventilation duration and ICU length of stay compared to physician-directed ad hoc weaning.

The rapid shallow breathing index (RSBI, f/Vt) below 105 breaths/min/L during spontaneous breathing remains a reliable physiological threshold to predict successful weaning, although cuff leak tests are necessary if laryngeal edema is suspected.

standard_knowledge.claim: The ATS/CHEST guideline conditionally suggests starting with a spontaneous breathing trial with inspiratory pressure augmentation (pressure support 5 to 8 cm H2O) rather than a T-piece or CPAP trial; this may increase extubation success.

In patients at high risk of extubation failure (hypercapnic COPD, age over 65, heart failure), post-extubation non-invasive ventilation or high-flow nasal cannula reduces post-extubation respiratory failure and reintubation.

uncertainties: Comparative re-intubation rates between high-flow nasal cannula alone versus alternating NIV with HFNC in mixed medical-surgical ICU extubation cohorts.
Utility of diaphragm ultrasound thickening fraction as an adjunct to standard RSBI in complex weaning failure.
mcq_angles: Calculation and interpretation of RSBI (respiratory rate divided by tidal volume in liters, threshold <105).
ATS/CHEST recommendation regarding SBT modality: preference for low-level pressure support over unassisted T-piece for initial SBT.
Indication for prophylactic post-extubation NIV in patients with chronic hypercapnia and underlying COPD.
case_hooks: A 68-year-old male with severe COPD intubated for 5 days for hypercapnic respiratory failure passing his SBT on PS 5/PEEP 5, prompting post-extubation respiratory support planning.
A 45-year-old trauma patient with prolonged intubation who exhibits absent cuff leak volume on deflation, raising concern for post-extubation stridor.

topic: lower GI bleeding

page.mentor_intro: Acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding (LGIB) ranges from self-limiting hematochezia to life-threatening hemorrhage. The 2023 ACG guidelines recommend objective risk stratification with the Oakland score to identify low-risk outpatients, restrictive blood transfusion thresholds, and early diagnostic CT angiography or colonoscopy in high-risk hemodynamic instability.

teaching_points.claim: A restrictive packed red blood cell transfusion strategy targeting a hemoglobin threshold of 7 g/dL (target 7 to 9 g/dL) is recommended for hemodynamically stable patients, improving survival and reducing rebleeding compared to liberal transfusion (threshold 9 g/dL).

In patients presenting with severe, ongoing hematochezia and hemodynamic instability, an upper endoscopy should be performed if an upper GI source is suspected, or immediate CT angiography should be utilized to localize active bleeding prior to catheter angiography and embolization.

For hospitalized patients requiring inpatient colonoscopy, the procedure should be performed following adequate oral colon lavage; early urgent colonoscopy (<24 hours) has not been shown to reduce rebleeding or mortality compared to elective next-day colonoscopy.

standard_knowledge.claim: The 2023 ACG clinical guideline on lower GI bleeding recommends using the validated Oakland score (threshold <= 8 points) to safely identify low-risk patients who can be discharged from the emergency department for outpatient investigation.

uncertainties: The exact clinical benefit and timing of colonoscopic through-the-scope clipping versus Doppler-guided endoscopic hemostasis in diverticular bleeding.
Optimal timing for restarting oral anticoagulation (DOACs vs warfarin) following acute lower GI bleed hemostasis in high thromboembolic risk patients.
mcq_angles: Clinical utility of the Oakland score: an Oakland score <= 8 safely identifies low-risk LGIB eligible for outpatient management.
Restrictive red blood cell transfusion threshold: transfusing only when hemoglobin drops below 7 g/dL (or below 8 g/dL in acute coronary syndrome).
Urgent diagnostic pathway for massive hematochezia with shock: ruling out brisk upper GI source or performing rapid CT angiography rather than unprepared urgent colonoscopy.

A 58-year-old female presenting with a single episode of dark red blood per rectum, normal vital signs, normal hemoglobin (13.5 g/dL), and an Oakland score of 6.

topic: lung cancer

page.mentor_intro: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related mortality. Population-level screening with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) reduces mortality, while comprehensive molecular profiling for actionable oncogenic driver mutations dictates first-line systemic therapy.

teaching_points.claim: The European NELSON trial confirmed a 24% to 26% reduction in lung cancer mortality at 10 years using volumetric low-dose CT nodule screening with low referral rates.

First-line osimertinib in EGFR-mutated NSCLC and alectinib in ALK-rearranged NSCLC significantly prolong progression-free and overall survival while providing superior central nervous system protection compared to early-generation TKIs.

standard_knowledge.claim: The randomized National Lung Screening Trial (NLST) demonstrated a 20% relative reduction in lung cancer mortality with annual low-dose CT screening compared to chest radiography in high-risk smokers.

In advanced non-small cell lung cancer, broad-panel next-generation sequencing is recommended before first-line therapy to find EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF V600E, RET, MET exon 14 and KRAS G12C alterations, which change treatment choice.

uncertainties: Optimal screening interval and risk prediction models for light or former smokers who quit > 15 years ago but retain substantial cumulative lifetime risk.
Overcoming acquired resistance to third-generation EGFR and ALK inhibitors driven by bypass track oncogene amplification (e.g. MET, HER2).
mcq_angles: Mortality reduction demonstrated by landmark LDCT screening trials (NLST 20%, NELSON ~24-26%).
Mandatory diagnostic step prior to checkpoint inhibitor therapy in adenocarcinoma: NGS testing to avoid fatal pneumonitis or poor efficacy in EGFR/ALK-mutated disease.
First-line targeted agent of choice for sensitizing EGFR mutations (exon 19 del / L858R): third-generation TKI osimertinib.

A 54-year-old female non-smoker presenting with cough and multiple bone metastases found to have lung adenocarcinoma harboring an EGFR exon 19 deletion.

topic: Lung cancer screening low-dose CT

page.mentor_intro: Low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) utilizes modern helical CT techniques to minimize radiation while identifying early-stage curable lung cancers. The implementation of standardized volumetric assessment and Lung-RADS reporting has dramatically reduced unnecessary invasive biopsy rates.

teaching_points.claim: The landmark NELSON trial demonstrated that volume-based CT screening with semi-automated nodule volume calculation and volume doubling time (VDT) yields an exceptionally low referral rate (2.1%) while reducing 10-year lung cancer mortality by 24% in men.

Subsolid (part-solid and pure ground-glass) nodules detected on LDCT exhibit indolent biology; guidelines mandate conservative observation with serial low-dose CT to document persistent growth or appearance of a solid component prior to resection.

standard_knowledge.claim: Lung-RADS grades screening CT findings from 1 (negative) to 4X (very suspicious); category 3 (probably benign) is managed with a 6-month repeat low-dose CT, and category 4 with further work-up such as PET/CT or tissue sampling.
A low-dose chest CT delivers roughly 1 to 1.5 mSv, compared with about 7 mSv for a standard diagnostic chest CT, so radiation risk per scan is small but cumulative over annual screening.

uncertainties: The long-term impact of artificial intelligence computer-aided detection (CAD) algorithms on reducing radiologist reading time and over-diagnosis rates.
Optimal biopsy technique (robotic bronchoscopy vs percutaneous transthoracic needle biopsy) for indeterminate Lung-RADS 4A peripheral nodules.
mcq_angles: Management of a Lung-RADS 3 nodule (solid nodule 6 to <8 mm at baseline): 6-month repeat low-dose CT scan.
Volume doubling time thresholds in the NELSON trial: VDT < 400 days indicates fast growth requiring pulmonology/oncology referral, whereas VDT > 600 days indicates benign indolence.
Diagnostic approach to pure ground-glass nodules < 30 mm: conservative annual LDCT follow-up rather than immediate biopsy due to slow doubling time.

A 64-year-old male found to have a 12 mm solid spiculated upper lobe nodule with pleural retraction (Lung-RADS 4B), requiring immediate diagnostic evaluation.

topic: Lupus Nephritis

page.mentor_intro: Lupus nephritis represents a severe manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus that leads to end-stage kidney disease if untreated. The KDIGO 2024 guidelines endorse early triple/multitarget therapy combining glucocorticoids and antimetabolites with belimumab or calcineurin inhibitors (voclosporin).

teaching_points.claim: The KDIGO 2024 clinical practice guidelines recommend initial treatment of active proliferative lupus nephritis (Class III/IV) with reduced-dose glucocorticoids plus mycophenolic acid analogs (or low-dose IV cyclophosphamide), with upfront addition of belimumab or voclosporin for triple therapy.

The AURORA 1 trial established that adding the novel calcineurin inhibitor voclosporin to mycophenolate mofetil and low-dose oral steroids significantly doubled complete renal response rates at 52 weeks (41% vs 23%, P<0.0001) without increasing nephrotoxicity.

standard_knowledge.claim: The landmark BLISS-LN phase 3 trial demonstrated that adding intravenous belimumab to standard of care significantly increased primary efficacy renal response at week 104 (43% vs 32%, P=0.03) and significantly reduced renal flare rates.

All patients with lupus nephritis should receive background hydroxychloroquine (unless strictly contraindicated) at a target dose not exceeding 5.0 mg/kg actual body weight to reduce renal flares and improve survival.

uncertainties: The direct comparative efficacy of belimumab-based triple therapy versus voclosporin-based triple therapy in patients with combined proliferative and membranous (Class IV+V) nephritis.
Safe duration of maintenance immunosuppression before considering a repeat 'protocol' kidney biopsy prior to drug withdrawal.
mcq_angles: Frontline induction regimens endorsed by KDIGO 2024: steroid + MMF + belimumab OR steroid + MMF + voclosporin for proliferative LN.
Baseline safety requirement for initiating voclosporin: baseline eGFR > 45 mL/min/1.73 m2.
Mandatory adjunctive pharmacotherapy in all SLE patients: hydroxychloroquine dosed <= 5 mg/kg actual body weight to reduce mortality and renal damage accrual.
case_hooks: A 26-year-old female with newly diagnosed biopsy-proven Class IV lupus nephritis and urine protein-to-creatinine ratio of 4.2 g/g evaluating upfront triple therapy options.
A 31-year-old male with active Class III+V lupus nephritis whose proteinuria remains 2.5 g/day despite 6 months of mycophenolate mofetil and prednisone.

topic: Lupus nephritis induction and maintenance therapy

page.mentor_intro: Induction and maintenance therapy for lupus nephritis aims to achieve rapid remission while preserving nephron mass and minimizing corticosteroid toxicity. Seminal trials (ALMS and MAINTAIN) established mycophenolate mofetil as equal or superior to cyclophosphamide for induction and maintenance.

teaching_points.claim: In the maintenance phase of the ALMS trial, mycophenolate mofetil was significantly superior to azathioprine in preventing renal relapse (HR 0.44, P=0.003) and treatment failure in patients who responded to induction.

The MAINTAIN Nephritis trial confirmed low-dose intravenous cyclophosphamide (Euro-Lupus regimen: 500 mg every 2 weeks for 6 doses) is equally effective as high-dose monthly NIH cyclophosphamide with significantly lower rates of severe infection and premature ovarian failure.
Maintenance immunosuppressive therapy for lupus nephritis must be continued for a minimum of 36 to 48 months following complete renal response before considering gradual taper.

standard_knowledge.claim: In the ALMS trial, mycophenolate mofetil (target 3 g/day) was not superior to monthly intravenous cyclophosphamide overall for induction (response about 56% versus 53%), with better responses in Black and Hispanic patients, so it is an accepted alternative first-line induction agent.

uncertainties: Optimal tapering schedule and timing for complete discontinuation of antimetabolite maintenance therapy in patients with prolonged (>5 years) complete clinical remission.
Efficacy of maintenance therapy in maintaining remission during planned pregnancy, balancing teratogenicity of MMF requiring a switch to azathioprine.
mcq_angles: Selection of induction therapy based on race/ethnicity from the ALMS trial: MMF demonstrated higher response rates than cyclophosphamide in Black and Hispanic patients.
Euro-Lupus regimen dosing: fixed 500 mg IV cyclophosphamide every 2 weeks for 6 doses (total 3 g) followed by azathioprine or MMF maintenance.
Pre-conception planning: discontinuing MMF at least 12 weeks prior to conception and transitioning to azathioprine (<= 2 mg/kg/day).

topic: Lyme Arthritis

page.mentor_intro: Lyme arthritis is a late-stage manifestation of Borrelia burgdorferi infection, typically presenting as monoarticular or oligoarticular inflammatory arthritis of large joints, predominantly the knee. Joint IDSA/AAN/ACR guidelines establish a 28-day oral antibiotic regimen as first-line therapy, reserving IV ceftriaxone for persistent non-responsive synovitis.

teaching_points.claim: The 2020 joint IDSA/AAN/ACR guidelines recommend an initial 28-day course of oral antibiotics (doxycycline 100 mg twice daily, amoxicillin 500 mg three times daily, or cefuroxime axetil 500 mg twice daily) as first-line therapy for Lyme arthritis.

If joint swelling and inflammation persist after an initial 28-day oral course, guidelines recommend either a second 28-day course of oral antibiotics or a 14- to 28-day course of intravenous ceftriaxone (2 g once daily).

Post-antibiotic (antibiotic-refractory) Lyme arthritis is defined as persistent joint inflammation despite appropriate oral and IV antibiotic therapy; further antibiotic courses are not recommended and treatment should transition to anti-inflammatory therapies (NSAIDs, DMARDs, or intra-articular corticosteroids).

standard_knowledge.claim: Diagnosis of Lyme arthritis rests on positive two-tier (or modified two-tier) serology in the right clinical setting; synovial fluid PCR for Borrelia DNA is often positive before antibiotics but is not required.

uncertainties: The optimal timing and selection of biologic DMARDs (e.g. TNF inhibitors) versus synovectomy in refractory post-infectious proliferative Lyme synovitis.
Diagnostic accuracy of Borrelia synovial fluid PCR in distinguishing active viable infection from persistent non-viable spirochetal DNA fragments.
mcq_angles: First-line treatment of choice for newly diagnosed Lyme arthritis: 28 days of oral doxycycline or amoxicillin.
Management of antibiotic-refractory Lyme arthritis: discontinuing antibiotics and initiating rheumatological anti-inflammatory therapy (NSAIDs, methotrexate, or intra-articular steroid injection).
Serological diagnosis in late Lyme disease: mandatory IgG Western blot confirmation (requiring at least 5 of 10 specific bands) alongside positive ELISA.
case_hooks: A 14-year-old boy in Connecticut presenting with a massive, minimally painful left knee effusion without systemic fever whose Lyme IgG Western blot is strongly positive.
A 45-year-old female whose knee swelling persists unchanged following 28 days of oral doxycycline and 28 days of IV ceftriaxone, with negative repeat synovial PCR.

topic: lyme disease diagnosis and treatment

page.mentor_intro: Accurate diagnosis of Lyme disease relies on stage-dependent clinical evaluation and validated two-tier laboratory algorithms. The CDC and FDA have approved modified two-tier testing (MTTT) utilizing sequential enzyme immunoassays (EIAs) including the C6 peptide, improving sensitivity in early disease without sacrificing specificity.

teaching_points.claim: The CDC and IDSA endorse modified two-tier testing (MTTT) protocols using two sequential enzyme immunoassays (EIAs) or chemiluminescent immunoassays (such as C6 peptide EIA) as an acceptable alternative to traditional Western blot second-tier testing.

Standard two-tier testing requires an initial sensitive EIA; if positive or equivocal, it is reflexed to a Western blot, requiring >= 2 of 3 bands on IgM Western blot (24, 39, 41 kDa) within the first 30 days of infection, or >= 5 of 10 bands on IgG Western blot after 30 days.
An isolated positive IgM Western blot in a patient with symptoms lasting more than 30 days represents a false-positive result and should not be used to support a diagnosis of chronic Lyme disease.

standard_knowledge.claim: Lyme serology (IgG antibodies) commonly remains positive for years or decades following successful curative treatment and does not reflect persistent active infection or require repeated antibiotic therapy.

uncertainties: Clinical utility of novel cellular immunity assays (e.g. interferon-gamma release assays for Borrelia) in distinguishing active reinfection from past resolved infection.
Pathophysiological mechanisms responsible for Post-Treatment Lyme Disease Syndrome (PTLDS) in patients with subjective symptoms persisting > 6 months post-treatment.
mcq_angles: Interpretation of Western blot criteria: IgM blot is valid only within the first 4 weeks of disease; IgG blot (>= 5 of 10 bands) is required after 30 days.
Advantages of modified two-tier testing (MTTT): eliminates subjective Western blot reading and increases sensitivity in early disseminated infection.
Clinical handling of persistent positive IgG titers post-treatment: titers persist indefinitely and do not indicate treatment failure or need for retreatment.

A 28-year-old female treated 3 years ago for erythema migrans who has routine lab work showing positive Lyme IgG antibodies, asking if she has recurrent infection.

topic: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis

page.mentor_intro: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM) is a rare, progressive, multi-system neoplastic disease primarily affecting women of childbearing age, characterized by cystic lung destruction, angiomyolipomas, and chylous effusions due to TSC1/TSC2 mutations. The landmark MILES trial established sirolimus (mTOR inhibitor) as the first disease-modifying therapy.

teaching_points.claim: The ATS/JRS clinical practice guidelines recommend sirolimus as first-line therapy for patients with LAM who have abnormal or declining lung function (FEV1 < 70% predicted or annual decline >= 90 mL/year), symptomatic chylous effusions, or renal angiomyolipomas > 4 cm.

standard_knowledge.claim: The randomized, double-blind MILES trial demonstrated that the mTOR inhibitor sirolimus stabilizes lung function decline (FEV1), reduces serum VEGF-D levels, and improves functional capacity and quality of life in patients with moderate-to-severe LAM.

In the MILES trial, the beneficial effects of sirolimus were suppressive rather than curative; upon cessation of sirolimus therapy, lung function decline resumed at a rate parallel to the placebo group, demonstrating the necessity of lifelong maintenance.

Serum vascular endothelial growth factor-D (VEGF-D) elevation (>= 800 pg/mL) in a patient with characteristic high-resolution chest CT cystic changes confirms the diagnosis of LAM without requiring lung biopsy.

uncertainties: Optimal target trough serum concentrations of sirolimus (e.g. low-dose 2-5 ng/mL vs standard 5-10 ng/mL) to balance long-term efficacy with mucosal and hematologic toxicities.
Safety and efficacy of combining mTOR inhibitors with autophagy inhibitors or hormonal therapies in rapidly progressing disease.
mcq_angles: Disease-modifying therapy of choice in LAM: mTOR inhibitor sirolimus (MILES trial).
Diagnostic non-invasive biomarker: serum VEGF-D >= 800 pg/mL in the setting of typical diffuse thin-walled pulmonary cysts on HRCT.
Consequence of stopping sirolimus: resumption of progressive FEV1 decline, requiring indefinite maintenance therapy.
case_hooks: A 32-year-old female presenting with recurrent spontaneous pneumothoraces and multiple bilateral thin-walled round cysts on chest CT whose serum VEGF-D is 1,250 pg/mL.
A 38-year-old woman with known sporadic LAM and an FEV1 of 62% predicted whose baseline spirometry confirms an annual FEV1 drop of 140 mL/year, prompting initiation of sirolimus.

topic: lymphoma

page.mentor_intro: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is the most common aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma. The landmark phase 3 POLARIX trial modified the decades-old standard-of-care R-CHOP regimen by demonstrating that Pola-R-CHP significantly improves progression-free survival in previously untreated intermediate- and high-risk patients.

teaching_points.claim: The randomized phase 3 POLARIX trial demonstrated that replacing vincristine with the anti-CD79b antibody-drug conjugate polatuzumab vedotin (Pola-R-CHP) significantly prolonged progression-free survival (HR 0.73, P=0.02) compared to standard R-CHOP in previously untreated DLBCL.

The International Prognostic Index (IPI score, based on age > 60, elevated LDH, ECOG >= 2, stage III/IV, and >1 extranodal site) risk-stratifies DLBCL patients to predict long-term complete response and survival.

Definitive diagnosis requires excisional lymph node biopsy rather than fine-needle aspiration to accurately assess nodal architecture, cell-of-origin (germinal center B-cell vs activated B-cell), and evaluate MYC/BCL2/BCL6 rearrangements (double-hit lymphoma).

standard_knowledge.claim: In patients with relapsed or refractory DLBCL within 12 months of first-line chemoimmunotherapy, CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy is preferred over salvage chemotherapy and autologous stem cell transplantation.

uncertainties: The incremental overall survival benefit of Pola-R-CHP over standard R-CHOP after extended 5- to 10-year follow-up across specific molecular subgroups.
The sequencing and optimal bridge therapies prior to commercial CAR-T cell manufacturing in rapidly progressive relapsed DLBCL.
mcq_angles: Intervention evaluated in the POLARIX trial: substitution of vincristine with polatuzumab vedotin (Pola-R-CHP), leading to superior progression-free survival.
Mandatory diagnostic biopsy technique for suspected lymphoma: excisional biopsy to provide adequate tissue for architecture and immunohistochemistry.
High-grade B-cell lymphoma definition: concurrent translocations involving MYC and BCL2 and/or BCL6 ('double-hit' or 'triple-hit' lymphoma) associated with poor prognosis.

topic: Male Breast Cancer

page.mentor_intro: Male breast cancer is an uncommon malignancy accounting for approximately 1% of all breast cancers, characterized by high rates of hormone-receptor positivity and strong associations with inherited cancer syndromes. The ASCO clinical practice guideline establishes tamoxifen as the standard adjuvant endocrine therapy.

teaching_points.claim: The ASCO clinical practice guideline recommends tamoxifen for an initial duration of 5 years as the standard adjuvant endocrine therapy for men with hormone receptor-positive early-stage breast cancer.

Aromatase inhibitor monotherapy is not recommended in men with breast cancer because inhibiting peripheral aromatase without testicular suppression triggers a pituitary feedback loop that increases LH, FSH, and testicular androgen/estrogen production.

If an aromatase inhibitor is required due to contraindications or intolerance to tamoxifen, it must be co-administered with a gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) analog (e.g. leuprolide) to suppress testicular steroidogenesis.

standard_knowledge.claim: Germline genetic counselling and testing (BRCA2 in particular, also BRCA1) should be offered to all men diagnosed with breast cancer, regardless of age or family history.

uncertainties: The incremental benefit of extending adjuvant tamoxifen to 10 years in men with node-positive or high-risk male breast cancer.

topic: Malignant Bowel Obstruction

page.mentor_intro: Malignant bowel obstruction (MBO) is a distressing complication of advanced intra-abdominal and pelvic malignancies, characterized by mechanical blockage, intestinal secretion, and visceral pain. Optimal timing for discontinuing dexamethasone trials if objective clinical resolution of obstruction is not observed within 5 days.

topic: Malignant hyperthermia and neuroleptic malignant syndrome: recognition and dantrolene

page.mentor_intro: Malignant hyperthermia (MH) and neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) are life-threatening hypermetabolic emergencies characterized by severe hyperthermia, muscle rigidity, and autonomic instability. The European Malignant Hyperthermia Group (EMHG) establishes protocols for rapid trigger removal and immediate intravenous dantrolene administration.

teaching_points.claim: Malignant hyperthermia is an inherited pharmacogenetic myopathy triggered by volatile inhalational anesthetics (sevoflurane, desflurane) or succinylcholine due to mutations in the ryanodine receptor (RYR1) causing uncontrolled myoplasmic calcium release.

Immediate management of malignant hyperthermia requires discontinuing all triggering volatile agents, hyperventilating with 100% oxygen at high flows, and administering intravenous dantrolene at an initial dose of 2.0 to 2.5 mg/kg repeated as necessary.

Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) is an idiosyncratic reaction triggered by central dopamine receptor antagonists (antipsychotics) characterized by 'lead-pipe' muscle rigidity, hyperthermia, autonomic instability, and marked creatine kinase elevation.

standard_knowledge.claim: Management of NMS requires immediate cessation of the offending neuroleptic, supportive care, and consideration of adjunctive therapy with the dopamine agonist bromocriptine or dantrolene to reduce severe muscle hypermetabolism.

uncertainties: The precise genetic overlap and shared calcium dysregulation mechanisms between idiopathic RYR1 variants and susceptibility to atypical neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
Comparative efficacy of rapid therapeutic plasma exchange versus high-dose dantrolene in severe, refractory NMS.

topic: Mallory-Weiss Syndrome

page.mentor_intro: Mallory-Weiss syndrome represents longitudinal mucosal lacerations at the gastroesophageal junction, typically triggered by forceful retching or vomiting. While the majority of mucosal tears heal spontaneously, active bleeding requires prompt endoscopic mechanical hemostasis using hemoclips or endoscopic band ligation.

teaching_points.claim: Endoscopic mechanical therapy with endoscopic hemoclips or endoscopic band ligation (EBL) is recommended as first-line therapy for actively bleeding Mallory-Weiss tears, achieving superior initial hemostasis and lower rebleeding rates compared to injection monotherapy.

Epinephrine injection monotherapy is insufficient for actively bleeding Mallory-Weiss tears due to high rebleeding rates and must always be combined with a mechanical modality (clips or band ligation).

Approximately 80% to 90% of Mallory-Weiss mucosal tears present with non-bleeding stigmata or clean-based ulcers that resolve spontaneously with conservative medical management and high-dose intravenous proton pump inhibitor therapy.

standard_knowledge.claim: Unlike Boerhaave syndrome, which represents full-thickness transmural esophageal rupture accompanied by mediastinitis and pneumomediastinum, Mallory-Weiss tears are non-transmural lacerations confined to the mucosa and submucosa.

uncertainties: Comparative clinical efficacy and safety of novel self-assembling peptide hemostatic gels versus through-the-scope hemoclips in retroflexed gastroesophageal junction tears.
Optimal duration of inpatient observation and PPI therapy following successful endoscopic mechanical hemostasis in patients with cirrhosis and coagulopathy.

Classic clinical presentation: sudden hematemesis following repeated episodes of non-bloody retching or vomiting, commonly after heavy alcohol intake.

topic: Malnutrition screening: MUST, NRS-2002, and nutritional support

page.mentor_intro: Disease-related malnutrition is a prevalent, under-recognized condition associated with prolonged hospital stays, infections, and increased mortality. The landmark EFFORT trial proved that systematic malnutrition screening using validated tools (NRS-2002, MUST) followed by individualized nutritional support significantly reduces hospital complications and all-cause mortality.

teaching_points.claim: The randomized multicenter EFFORT trial in The Lancet (over 2,000 medical inpatients) established that individualized nutritional support in patients identified at nutritional risk (NRS-2002 score >= 3) significantly reduced 30-day all-cause mortality (7.2% vs 9.9%, P=0.015) and major adverse clinical complications.

The Nutritional Risk Screening 2002 (NRS-2002) and Malnutrition Universal Screening Tool (MUST) are validated clinical screening instruments recommended by ESPEN and ASPEN to screen all hospitalized medical patients within 24 to 48 hours of admission.

The Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM) consensus criteria require at least one phenotypic criterion (weight loss, low BMI, or reduced muscle mass) and one etiologic criterion (reduced intake/assimilation or systemic inflammation) to establish a formal diagnosis of malnutrition.

standard_knowledge.claim: Nutritional support protocols should target 25 to 30 kcal/kg/day and 1.2 to 1.5 g/kg/day of protein, while monitoring for refeeding syndrome (hypophosphatemia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia) during the first 72 hours of nutritional reintroduction in severely malnourished patients.

uncertainties: The cost-effectiveness of continuing high-protein oral nutritional supplements for 6 months post-hospital discharge in sarcopenic elderly patients.
Optimal timing and clinical benefits of early parenteral nutrition supplementation when enteral intake achieves <50% of caloric goals by day 4.

topic: management of acute intermittent porphyria

page.mentor_intro: Acute intermittent porphyria (AIP) is an autosomal dominant inborn error of heme biosynthesis resulting from porphobilinogen deaminase (PBGD) deficiency. Neurotoxic accumulation of ALA and PBG triggers acute neurovisceral attacks. Management centers on prompt intravenous hemin for acute crises and monthly subcutaneous givosiran for recurrent attack prophylaxis.

teaching_points.claim: The randomized phase 3 ENVISION trial in NEJM demonstrated that the hepatic ALAS1-directed RNA interference therapeutic givosiran reduced the annualized attack rate of acute intermittent porphyria by 74% compared to placebo.

Intravenous hemin (3 to 4 mg/kg/day for 4 days) is the first-line disease-specific treatment for acute neurovisceral porphyria attacks, acting via negative feedback to downregulate ALAS1 and halt neurotoxic metabolite accumulation.

Acute attacks present with severe, poorly localized abdominal pain out of proportion to physical findings, accompanied by autonomic hyperactivity (hypertension, tachycardia), peripheral motor neuropathy, and dark reddish-brown urine that darkens on light exposure.

standard_knowledge.claim: High carbohydrate intake (oral or IV 10% dextrose) suppresses hepatic ALAS1 activity through the PGC-1alpha pathway and serves as a supportive temporizing measure in mild attacks or while awaiting hemin delivery.

uncertainties: Long-term renal function trajectories and chronic kidney disease risk in patients receiving chronic maintenance givosiran therapy.
Surveillance protocols for early detection of hepatocellular carcinoma in patients with AIP and recurrent biochemically active disease.

topic: management of HF eith Reduced ejection fraction

page.mentor_intro: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) is characterized by left ventricular ejection fraction <= 40% and progressive neurohormonal maladaptation. Modern guidelines from ESC and ACC/AHA mandate rapid simultaneous or sequential initiation of four foundational pillars of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT).

teaching_points.claim: Initiation of all four foundational classes reduces 2-year all-cause mortality by over 60% compared to conventional untreated historical cohorts or mono/dual therapy.

standard_knowledge.claim: The 2021 ESC and 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA guidelines recommend four foundational drug classes for HFrEF: an ACE inhibitor or ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan), an evidence-based beta-blocker, a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, and an SGLT2 inhibitor.
Beta-blocker therapy in HFrEF must be restricted to the three agents with proven survival benefit in randomized trials: carvedilol, sustained-release metoprolol succinate, and bisoprolol.

Loop diuretics (furosemide, bumetanide, torsemide) are essential to treat and maintain euvolemia, but their doses should be titrated to the minimum required because diuretics do not confer mortality reduction.

uncertainties: Optimal sequencing strategy: simultaneous low-dose initiation of all four classes within 48 to 72 hours of admission versus rapid step-wise escalation over 4 to 6 weeks.
Management of worsening renal function and transient eGFR drops (>30%) following combined ARNI and SGLT2 inhibitor introduction.

Specific beta-blockers with proven survival reduction in HFrEF: carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, and bisoprolol (atenolol and metoprolol tartrate are not guideline-recommended).
Targeting euvolemia: loop diuretics alleviate symptoms and volume overload but do not modify long-term mortality.

topic: Mantle Cell Lymphoma

page.mentor_intro: Mantle Cell Lymphoma (MCL) is an incurable B-cell malignancy characterized by the t(11;14) translocation and cyclin D1 overexpression. The landmark TRIANGLE trial by the European MCL Network has transformed frontline management by demonstrating that adding the BTK inhibitor ibrutinib significantly improves failure-free survival and challenges the necessity of upfront autologous transplantation.

teaching_points.claim: The randomized phase 3 TRIANGLE trial in The Lancet established that incorporating the BTK inhibitor ibrutinib into frontline immunochemotherapy and maintenance significantly prolonged failure-free survival (3-year FFS 88% vs 72%, HR 0.52) compared to standard chemoimmunotherapy plus autologous stem-cell transplantation (ASCT).

In the TRIANGLE trial, ibrutinib-containing therapy without ASCT demonstrated non-inferiority and superior failure-free survival compared to standard chemoimmunotherapy with ASCT, questioning the mandatory role of upfront transplantation in younger patients.

Pathologically, mantle cell lymphoma is characterized by the pathognomonic t(11;14)(q13;q32) translocation resulting in CCND1-IGH fusion and constitutive cyclin D1 nuclear overexpression, with blastoid or pleomorphic variants conferring an aggressive course.

standard_knowledge.claim: Mantle cell lymphoma with TP53 mutation or 17p deletion has a poor response to standard intensive chemoimmunotherapy and autologous transplant; BTK inhibitor-based regimens, clinical trials or CAR T-cell therapy are preferred strategies.

Long-term cardiovascular safety and atrial fibrillation incidence associated with multi-year continuous BTK inhibitor maintenance.

topic: MASLD

page.mentor_intro: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) represents hepatic steatosis in the presence of at least one cardiometabolic risk factor. The landmark MAESTRO-NASH trial established resmetirom, a thyroid hormone receptor-beta selective agonist, as the first FDA-approved disease-modifying therapy capable of resolving NASH and reversing liver fibrosis.

teaching_points.claim: The randomized phase 3 MAESTRO-NASH trial in NEJM demonstrated that the thyroid hormone receptor-beta selective agonist resmetirom achieved both NASH resolution with no worsening of fibrosis (25.9% to 29.9% vs 9.7%) and fibrosis improvement of at least one stage (24.2% to 25.9% vs 14.2%) compared to placebo.

Resmetirom selectively targets hepatic thyroid hormone receptor-beta (THR-beta) to stimulate mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation and lipophagy while avoiding extrahepatic THR-alpha adverse effects on heart rate and bone density.

Non-invasive fibrosis assessment algorithms (such as FIB-4 score followed by transient elastography or magnetic resonance elastography) are recommended to identify at-risk MASH patients with significant fibrosis (stage F2-F3) who qualify for therapeutic intervention.

standard_knowledge.claim: Cardiometabolic comorbidities (type 2 diabetes, obesity, dyslipidemia) represent the primary drivers of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in MASLD, necessitating aggressive lifestyle intervention, statins, and incretin-based metabolic therapies.

topic: MDS with Ring Sideroblasts

page.mentor_intro: Myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) with ring sideroblasts are clonal stem cell disorders characterized by ineffective erythropoiesis, transfusion-dependent anemia, and somatic mutations in SF3B1. Luspatercept acts as a recombinant fusion protein ligand trap for GDF11 and other TGF-beta superfamily ligands, inhibiting downstream SMAD2/3 signaling and releasing late-stage erythroid differentiation arrest.

Somatic mutations in the spliceosome gene SF3B1 are detected in over 80% to 90% of MDS with ring sideroblasts, strongly correlating with the presence of mitochondrial iron accumulation and favorable lower-risk clinical biology.

topic: Mechanical ventilation modes: volume control, pressure control, SIMV, PSV

page.mentor_intro: Understanding ventilator modes is essential for matching mechanical support to patient respiratory mechanics and synchrony. Volume control guarantees minute ventilation, pressure control limits peak alveolar pressure, synchronized intermittent mandatory ventilation (SIMV) mixes mandatory and spontaneous breaths, and pressure support ventilation (PSV) facilitates weaning.

teaching_points.claim: In volume-controlled ventilation, tidal volume and inspiratory flow are preset and guaranteed, while peak inspiratory pressure varies directly with changes in respiratory system compliance and airway resistance.

In pressure-controlled ventilation, inspiratory pressure and inspiratory time are fixed, producing a decelerating flow pattern that limits peak airway pressures, while delivered tidal volume varies according to lung compliance and patient effort.

Synchronized intermittent mandatory ventilation (SIMV) has been shown in clinical trials to prolong the duration of mechanical ventilation and weaning compared to once-daily spontaneous breathing trials or pressure support titration.

standard_knowledge.claim: Pressure support is a patient-triggered, pressure-limited, flow-cycled mode in which the patient controls rate and inspiratory time; it is commonly used for weaning and spontaneous breathing trials.

uncertainties: The physiological superiority and patient-ventilator synchrony benefits of neurally adjusted ventilatory assist (NAVA) versus standard proportional assist ventilation (PAV).
Optimal flow-cycling termination criteria (e.g. 25% vs 40% of peak inspiratory flow) in obstructive lung disease to prevent auto-PEEP during pressure support.
mcq_angles: Primary variable that fluctuates during volume-control ventilation when lung compliance worsens: peak inspiratory and plateau pressures rise.
Cycling mechanism of Pressure Support Ventilation (PSV): flow-cycled (inspiration terminates when inspiratory flow decays to a preset percentage of peak flow).
Clinical drawback of SIMV in weaning: increases work of breathing and prolongs weaning duration compared to daily pressure support SBT protocols.
case_hooks: A 62-year-old male on volume-control ventilation whose peak airway pressure alarm sounds following acute right mainstem bronchus intubation.
A 50-year-old female with COPD on pressure support ventilation exhibiting expiratory muscle contraction and premature cycling, indicating patient-ventilator dyssynchrony.

topic: melanoma

page.mentor_intro: Advanced cutaneous melanoma has been revolutionized by immune checkpoint inhibition and targeted BRAF/MEK kinase inhibitors. Landmark 10-year outcomes from the CheckMate 067 trial in NEJM established that combination dual immunotherapy with nivolumab plus ipilimumab yields durable long-term overall survival and potential cure.

teaching_points.claim: The 10-year final outcomes of the randomized CheckMate 067 trial in NEJM demonstrated a median overall survival of 71.9 months with nivolumab plus ipilimumab compared to 36.9 months with nivolumab alone and 19.9 months with ipilimumab alone in advanced melanoma.

At 10 years, 43% of patients in the nivolumab plus ipilimumab group remained alive, with durable treatment-free intervals confirming the potential for long-term functional cure in metastatic melanoma.

In patients harboring activating BRAF V600 mutations (present in ~40-50% of cutaneous melanomas), targeted combination therapy with a BRAF inhibitor (dabrafenib, encorafenib) plus MEK inhibitor (trametinib, binimetinib) achieves rapid tumor regression with objective response rates > 65%.

standard_knowledge.claim: Breslow tumor thickness (in millimeters) and ulceration remain the two most important primary histological prognostic determinants of sentinel lymph node metastasis and overall survival in localized cutaneous melanoma.

uncertainties: The optimal first-line sequencing strategy in BRAF-mutated metastatic melanoma: upfront dual immunotherapy (nivolumab + ipilimumab) versus upfront targeted therapy (BRAF/MEK inhibitors) versus sandwich 'induction-switch' protocols (DREAMseq trial).
Management of late immune-related adverse events and optimal duration of immunotherapy in patients achieving complete radiological remission at 2 years.
mcq_angles: Landmark survival result of the CheckMate 067 trial: median overall survival of nearly 6 years (71.9 months) and 43% 10-year survival with dual checkpoint inhibition.
Primary histological prognostic factor in early melanoma: Breslow depth measured from the granular layer of the epidermis to the deepest tumor cell.
Standard targeted therapy combination for BRAF V600-mutated melanoma: combining a BRAF inhibitor with a MEK inhibitor to delay resistance and prevent paradoxical secondary skin squamous carcinomas.

A 55-year-old female with a 2.4 mm Breslow thickness, ulcerated superficial spreading melanoma on her back undergoing wide local excision (2 cm margins) and sentinel lymph node biopsy.

topic: Membranous Nephropathy

page.mentor_intro: Membranous nephropathy (MN) is the leading cause of primary nephrotic syndrome in non-diabetic Caucasian adults. Autoantibodies against the M-type phospholipase A2 receptor (PLA2R) account for 70% to 80% of primary cases. The landmark MENTOR trial in NEJM established rituximab as non-inferior to cyclosporine at 12 months and superior in maintaining durable 24-month remission.

teaching_points.claim: The randomized MENTOR trial in NEJM demonstrated that rituximab was noninferior to cyclosporine in inducing complete or partial remission of proteinuria at 12 months (60% vs 52%) and significantly superior at 24 months (60% vs 20%, P<0.001) due to high relapse rates upon cyclosporine withdrawal.

Circulating anti-PLA2R autoantibodies are present in 70% to 80% of patients with primary membranous nephropathy; serum anti-PLA2R titers correlate directly with disease activity, predict response to therapy, and immunological remission (antibody clearance) precedes clinical proteinuria reduction by months.

The KDIGO 2021 guidelines risk-stratify membranous nephropathy into moderate, high, and very high risk based on proteinuria, eGFR, and anti-PLA2R levels, recommending rituximab or cyclical cyclophosphamide/steroids (Ponticelli regimen) for high-risk patients.

standard_knowledge.claim: Membranous nephropathy confers a uniquely high risk of venous thromboembolism (particularly renal vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism) when serum albumin is < 2.0 to 2.5 g/dL, justifying prophylactic anticoagulation based on bleeding risk calculations.

uncertainties: The comparative clinical efficacy and safety of upfront combination therapy (rituximab plus low-dose cyclophosphamide) versus sequential monotherapy in patients with very high anti-PLA2R titers (>150 RU/mL).
Utility of anti-THSD7A, anti-NELL-1, and anti-SEMA3B autoantibodies in guiding secondary malignancy screening protocols.
mcq_angles: Primary finding of the MENTOR trial: rituximab demonstrated clear superiority over cyclosporine in maintaining 24-month proteinuria remission.
Diagnostic non-invasive utility of anti-PLA2R antibodies: high titer in a nephrotic patient with preserved eGFR can confirm primary MN and avoid kidney biopsy in selected cases.
Specific thrombotic complication strongly associated with membranous nephropathy: renal vein thrombosis, presenting with sudden flank pain, macroscopic hematuria, and acute kidney injury.
case_hooks: A 46-year-old male with nephrotic syndrome (proteinuria 9.5 g/day, albumin 1.8 g/dL), high-titer anti-PLA2R antibodies (240 RU/mL), and normal renal function, evaluated for frontline rituximab therapy.
A 52-year-old female with membranous nephropathy and serum albumin 1.9 g/dL who develops sudden left flank pain and gross hematuria, found to have acute left renal vein thrombosis on CT angiography.
